**Description:**

The figure illustrates a decision flow for managing temperature excursions affecting 2-8°C products within a pharmaceutical supply chain. It begins with a data logger alarm indicating a temperature outside the acceptable 2-8°C range. If an excursion exceeding 8°C occurs for more than 2 hours cumulatively, the product is quarantined (held) and QA is notified within 4 hours.  Further evaluation is then conducted to determine if any readings were above 25°C or if the product was frozen (below 0°C), and if either of these conditions are met, the lot is rejected, followed by a stability review by QA.

**Description:**

The figure illustrates a cold chain distribution network for a pharmaceutical product, showing the flow of goods between four locations: a Manufacturing Site in Durham, NC; a Central DC in Memphis, TN; a West Hub in Reno, NV; and an East Hub in Allentown, PA.  Three distinct lanes (L1, L2, and L3) are depicted, each with a specified transportation time and method – Lane L1 uses a PCM shipper for 96 hours, Lane L2 uses a PCM shipper for 120 hours, and Lane L3 uses an active container for 1 day.  Data loggers record information every 10 minutes, and during the summer months (June-September), a 20% increase in coolant mass is utilized for the summer lanes.
